questions.question: What does it mean that a maximization linear program has an unbounded objective?
options: The feasible region extends without limit in some direction
No feasible solution satisfies all of the constraints
The optimum is attained at more than one corner point
Feasible solutions reach values above every finite bound

questions.question: For a minimization linear program, which situation is called an unbounded objective?
options: Feasible objective values can be made arbitrarily negative
Feasible objective values can be made arbitrarily large
Every variable can be made arbitrarily large while feasible
The minimum is attained only at the origin of the region

questions.question: In a feasible maximization tableau written as $z+\sum_j q_jx_j=z_0$, which pattern in the column of a nonbasic variable $x_k$ certifies an unbounded objective?
options: $q_k<0$ and no strictly positive entry in the constraint rows
$q_k<0$ and at least one negative entry in the constraint rows
$q_k>0$ while every entry below it is zero or negative
$q_k<0$ and the largest right-hand side in its own row

questions.question: Which statement correctly separates an unbounded linear program from a linear program with no feasible solution?
options: Both have no feasible solution; they differ only in the region
The unbounded one has feasible solutions; the other has none
The unbounded one has no feasible solution; the other has many
Both have feasible solutions, but neither has a finite optimum

questions.question: A company's profit model is solved and reports an unbounded objective. What is the most sensible first reaction?
options: Look for a missing restriction, such as a capacity limit
Report that the company can earn unlimited profit
Conclude that the model has no feasible plan at all
Rerun the same model, as the result is a rounding error

questions.question: For $\max\ 2x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1-x_2\le4$ (slack $s_1$), $x_1\le6$ (slack $s_2$) and $x_1,x_2\ge0$, two pivots give the feasible tableau $z-s_1+3s_2=14$, $x_1+s_2=6$ (basic $x_1$), $x_2-s_1+s_2=2$ (basic $x_2$). What does this tableau show?
options: The tableau is optimal: all right-hand sides are nonnegative
$s_1$ enters and can rise to $2$, limited by the row of $x_2$
$s_2$ enters, since it has the largest objective coefficient
The objective is unbounded: $s_1$ can enter and rise freely

questions.question: For $\max\ 2x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1-x_2\le4$ (slack $s_1$), $x_1\le6$ (slack $s_2$) and $x_1,x_2\ge0$, two pivots give the feasible tableau $z-s_1+3s_2=14$, $x_1+s_2=6$ (basic $x_1$), $x_2-s_1+s_2=2$ (basic $x_2$). Keeping $s_2=0$ and setting $s_1=t\ge0$, which feasible points $(x_1,x_2)$ does the tableau give?
For $\max\ 3x_1+2x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\ge10$, $x_1-x_2\le2$ and $x_1,x_2\ge0$, which family of points shows that the objective is unbounded?
In a feasible maximization tableau, an improving nonbasic variable has only zero or negative entries in its column. Why does no row limit its increase?
options: The basic variables decrease, but never below their own values
Its ratios are negative, and negative ratios mean no limit
No basic variable decreases as it rises, so none reaches zero
The objective value limits the increase instead of the rows

questions.question: The feasible region of a maximization LP extends without limit in some direction. Which statement about its objective is correct?
options: It must be unbounded, as the region itself is unbounded
It may still have a finite optimum for this objective
It must have a finite optimum, since the region is nonempty
It must have no optimum, as no corner point is the last one

questions.question: For $\max\ 2x_1+x_3$ subject to $x_1-x_3\le4$ (slack $s_1$), $2x_1\le10$ (slack $s_2$), $x_1,x_3\ge0$, the initial tableau is $z-2x_1-x_3=0$, $x_1-x_3+s_1=4$, $2x_1+s_2=10$. What can be concluded from this tableau already?
options: Nothing yet: $x_1$ is most improving and must enter first
The objective is bounded: $2x_1\le10$ limits $x_1$ to $5$
The objective is unbounded: $x_1$ has the most negative coefficient
The objective is unbounded: raising $x_3$ alone is never limited

questions.question: For $\max\ x_1+a x_2$ subject to $x_1-x_2\le2$, $x_1\le5$ and $x_1,x_2\ge0$, where $a$ is a real parameter, for which values of $a$ is the objective unbounded?
options: Exactly for $a\ge0$
Exactly for $a>1$
Exactly for $a>0$
Exactly for $a<0$

questions.question: In a feasible maximization tableau, the improving entering variable $x_3$ has entries $-2$, $0$, $-1$ in rows with right-hand sides $6$, $3$, $5$. How far can $x_3$ increase while all basic values stay nonnegative?
options: To $3$: the first row gives the ratio $6/2$
To $0$: the zero entry blocks any increase
No limit: $6+2x_3$, $3$, $5+x_3$ never fall
To $5$: the last row allows at most $5/1$

questions.question: For $\max\ 2x_2$ subject to $x_1\le3$, $x_1\ge5$ and $x_1,x_2\ge0$, a student writes $x_1+s_1=3$, $-x_1+s_2=-5$ with basic $s_1,s_2$ and objective row $z-2x_2=0$. Since the column of $x_2$ has no positive entry, she declares the objective unbounded. Which assessment is correct?
options: Right: $x_2$ is improving and no entry in its column is positive
Wrong: $x_2$ has only zero entries, so it is not allowed to enter
Wrong: here $s_2=-5$, and the program has no feasible solution at all
Wrong: the certificate needs every objective coefficient to be negative

questions.question: For $\max\ 3x_1+2x_2$ subject to $x_1-x_2\le4$, $x_1+x_2\ge2$, $x_2\le8$ and $x_1,x_2\ge0$, which statement is correct?
options: Since $x_1\le4$, the best value is $28$ at $(4,8)$
The maximum is finite, $52$, attained at $(12,8)$
It is unbounded, as each $(t,0)$ with $t\ge2$ is feasible
Profit grows without limit along $(t,8)$, $t\ge0$

questions.question: A profit model $\max\ 5x_1+4x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\ge20$ and $x_1,x_2\ge0$ is unbounded. Which single added constraint gives a finite maximum?
In a feasible maximization tableau $z+\sum_j q_jx_j=z_0$, the nonbasic $x_4$ has $q_4=2$ and only negative entries in the constraint rows. What follows from this column alone?
options: The objective is unbounded, since $x_4$ can rise without limit
No unboundedness certificate, since $x_4$ does not improve $z$
The tableau has no feasible solution, since all entries are negative
The tableau is optimal, since raising $x_4$ cannot improve $z$

questions.question: A maximization LP with $\boldsymbol{x}\ge\boldsymbol{0}$ has a nonempty feasible region in which every variable is at most some fixed number $M$. Can its objective be unbounded?
options: Yes: a region with infinitely many points allows endless growth
Yes: if one objective coefficient is larger than all the others
No: a bounded region always has exactly one optimal corner point
No: with $0\le x_j\le M$ a linear objective is bounded too
